plot: The morning after Clementine the purple tractor arrives a week early with eight gold stars, Turbo can't believe a slow tractor has never lost a race; Clementine only says 'fast has nothing to do with it', her one lap leaves a single unbroken track between the white lines while Turbo's lap skids and stops, Turbo spies her 'slower, never stop' lesson and makes Pip zoom out of the lines, and Bolt, remembering Grandma Rosa's 'steady, never stopping', realises race nine is a slow race where the last car wins; Turbo learns to drive slowly and loses the practice race happily, then Pip says something knocks on her roof every night and nobody is there.

script.title: A Tractor Who Never Lost a Race?!
script.description: Clementine the tractor has never lost a race. Inspector Bolt finds out how. Inspector Bolt #35

set.place: the Wheelburg school sports field with its white-lined track and the yard behind the school, a windy autumn morning until evening

beats.say: Lap ninety-nine! Watch me, Clementine! Zoom, zoom, zoom!
Very fast, dear. But you would still lose race number nine.
LOSE?! To a tractor? You're slower than a snail!
It was the morning after Clementine rolled into Wheelburg. A week early.
She carried eight gold stars. One for every race she ever drove.
Eight races and eight wins? You never lost, Clementine?
Never once, little one. Your Grandma Rosa lost to me twice!
But how? I'm the fastest car in all of Wheelburg!
That's the secret, dear. Fast has nothing to do with it.
Nothing to do with it? Racing is ALL about fast!
A real mystery, then. How does a tractor win every race?
Easy. Everybody else fell asleep waiting for her.
Grumpy! Be nice! She's our guest!
I won't tell my secret. A racer never does.
But my tracks will tell you, Inspector. Watch me closely.
So Clementine drove one lap of the school field. Very... very... slowly.
Is she even moving? I can't tell!
She's moving, Turbo. Like the little hand on a clock.
Look! She never stopped. Not even once!
Interesting. And she stayed between the two white lines.
Boring! My turn! Now watch a REAL lap!
Turbo zoomed so fast that he cut the corner across the grass.
Done! Forty seconds flat! Beat THAT, Clementine!
Lovely, dear. But in race nine, you would be out.
OUT?! I came first! Bolt, that's not fair!
Procedure, Turbo. First, we read the tracks.
Two lines of tracks went all the way round the field.
Clementine's tracks are one long line. No gaps at all.
And Turbo's tracks jump, skid and stop. Three times.
Those are my cool stopping skids! Everybody loves them!
The grass doesn't.
If I can't work this out, I'll lose race nine!
And Grandma Rosa is coming all this way to watch you.
So Turbo did what any racer would do. He spied.
Shh. Agent Turbo is on the case. Very sneaky.
Behind the school, Clementine was giving a lesson. To Pip!
Slower, Pip. Even slower. But never stop.
Slower? This is so hard! My wheels want to zoom!
She's teaching Pip to be SLOW? That must be a trick!
Don't listen, Pip! Real racers go FAST!
Pip zoomed. Pip wobbled. And Pip rolled right over the white line.
Oops! Clementine, I'm out now, aren't I?
Out of the lines means out of the race, little one.
Out? For going fast? This race is upside down!
An upside-down race. Finally, a race I'd like.
Wait. Say that again, Turbo. Upside down.
Bolt rolled slowly along Clementine's long, unbroken track.
No stops. Inside the lines. And never, ever in a hurry.
Turbo, what did Grandma Rosa's letter say about her old race?
Steady. Never stopping. I thought it meant a really long race!
Bolt, you have your thinking face on! Tell us!
It's not a long race. It's a SLOW race.
The LAST car across the line wins. But you may never stop.
Stop once, or leave the lines, and you're out.
Right you are, Inspector. Nine races, and I'm always the slowest!
So my zooms, my skids, my cool corners...
Would get you out in three seconds.
I trained a whole week the wrong way! Race nine is ruined!
Not ruined, Turbo! We can both learn it. Together!
Lesson one, dear. Feel every little bump in the grass.
So Turbo tried to drive slowly. For the very first time.
Slow... slow... oh, my engine is so bored!
He stopped. He wobbled. His wheel nearly touched the line.
Breathe, Turbo! Look at the leaves, not at the finish!
Leaves. Okay. One red leaf. One yellow leaf...
And slowly, slowly, Turbo began to smile.
Hey! Going slow, I can see everything! Birds! The bakery!
Practice race! Turbo, Clementine and me! Last one wins!
Ready... steady... slowly!
Three racers crawled toward the finish. Nobody made a sound.
This is the most exciting thing I have ever watched.
Pip crossed first. Then Turbo. Then, last of all, Clementine.
Nine races, still never lost! But you did well, dear.
I lost slowly. Best losing ever!
Wheelburg's slowest racers! Hooray!
Remember, everyone: never judge a racer by its wheels.
Or a tractor by its speed!
But that evening, Pip rolled up to Bolt very quietly.
Bolt, something knocks on my roof. Every night. Knock, knock, knock.
Every night? And who is knocking, Pip?
That's the thing. Nobody is ever there!
What do you think Bolt will find next time? We'll find out in the next episode!
